transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-13 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Lina Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Jamal Price (Redwood SE), Rina Sato (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (Cascade CTO), Tom Reynolds (Cascade ML Eng), Aisha Khan (Cascade Infra), Ben Hsu (Cascade Product)
---
Summary: quick discovery focused on streaming p95 SLOs and how Redwood hosted vs dedicated/private options handle concurrent token flows, KV cache, and fallback policies. Customer is sensitive to sustained burst and streaming token/sec for real-time summarization product.

[00:00:05] Lina: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we wanted to make sure we understand your streaming SLA targets and the traffic profile, so we can recommend hosted vs dedicated. quick intros?
[00:00:18] Priya: hey, im priya, cto at cascade, we run a realtime summarization and alerting system for financial news, so latency matters.
[00:00:25] Tom: tom, ml eng, ive been doing model integration and perf tests. we care about p95 under 350ms for short summaries (~80-150 tokens) and about 1.2s p95 for longer 512 token flows when streaming.
[00:00:40] Aisha: infra here, i've got concerns around VPC/egress control and key management, also cost predictability.
[00:00:45] Lina: great, that gives us a good baseline. Marcus, quick overview?
[00:00:50] Marcus: sure, so at a high level redwood supports hosted api, dedicated pools and private vpc deployments. for streaming we look at token/sec and prefix/KV cache to shave p95. we typically measure p95 both for first-byte and end-of-stream.
[00:01:10] Tom: first byte p95 is important for us — we need sub-200ms when model is warm for the short prompts, burstiness is a problem, spikes up to 300 concurrent streams during earnings windows.
[00:01:25] Jamal: ok, and are those 300 concurrent active streams or 300k requests per minute?
[00:01:30] Tom: more like 300 concurrent long-polling streams, average token generation rates at 15-20 tok/sec per stream for longer summaries, short ones are 40-60 tok/sec but only for ~100 tokens.
[00:01:45] [00:02:10] Priya: and our target is to keep p95 end-to-end for the summary API under 1s for almost all cases — we have SLA commitments to our enterprise customers.
[00:02:22] Marcus: got it. couple things to clarify: are you open to dedicated reserved capacity for predictable p95, or do you prefer hosted with fallback strategies to cheaper variants?
[00:02:33] Priya: we want predictable p95. willing to look at dedicated if the cost math works and if we can do private networking for compliance.
[00:02:42] Aisha: plus KMS integration and audit logs, we need key separation and HSM-backed policies ideally.
[00:02:50] Lina: Redwood supports KMS integrations and has audit logs + RBAC; for private we can do customer-managed control plane and on-prem option. we'll send the security pack after this call.
[00:03:00] 
[00:03:15] Tom: can you explain how batch vs streaming execution changes per-token latency? like whats the delta if we enable batching for peak throughput?
[00:03:25] Marcus: yeah so batching smooths GPU utilization and drops cost per token — but it increases queuing latency depending on batch windows. our runtime supports adaptive continuous batching where we set a micro-window (5-15ms) for low-latency workloads to keep p95 impact small. for streaming, we also optimize attention kernels and kv cache so incremental token generation is faster.
[00:03:55] Ben: kv cache — does redwood share kv cache across requests or is it per-session?
[00:04:02] Jamal: it's per session for correctness, but we have prefix caching where common prompt prefixes can be cached and reused across sessions which helps for template-driven prompts. that reduces compute and drops p95.
[00:04:20] Tom: curious about quantization and its impact on p95 for streaming? we have looked at int8 and int4.
[00:04:28] Marcus: quantization reduces memory and can improve throughput for larger batches; for low-latency streaming the improvements are mixed — int8 often helps, int4 can be noisy depending on the model. we recommend benchmark runs.
[00:04:40] 
[00:05:10] Priya: what about fallback model policies? during big spikes we want graceful degradation not hard failures.
[00:05:18] Lina: redwood has routing policies — you can route by latency, cost, or region. during capacity constraints you can failover to a compatible smaller variant or to a cached response. we can set canary rollouts and automatic fallback thresholds.
[00:05:35] Aisha: are there cold-start penalties when scaling up dedicated pools? if we scale from zero to handle spikes?
[00:05:45] Marcus: reserved capacity usually avoids that - autoscaling policies can do warm pools with burst capacity; cold-starts can add 1-2s to warm up a GPU depending on model size. for strict p95 targets we recommend a baseline reserved capacity.
[00:06:00] Tom: what about token/sec per GPU numbers — ballpark?
[00:06:05] Jamal: depends on model, sequence length, and kernel choices. for a mid-sized Llama-like family on A100-ish perf, you might see sustained 6-10k tokens/sec per GPU with good batching; for streaming low-latency scenarios single-stream throughput is low but aggregate across GPU matters. we'll run an exact benchmark with your prompt shapes.
[00:06:25] 
[00:07:00] Priya: ok our compliance asks: do you have SOC2, iso27001? how granular are the audit logs?
[00:07:08] Lina: yes we are SOC2 compliant, and we can provide SOC2 report; audit logs are token-level invocation logs with redaction options. for private deployments audit logs can be exported to your SIEM.
[00:07:20] Aisha: SSO/SAML? fine grained RBAC?
[00:07:24] Rina: yes SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC with scopes, and per-team quotas.
[00:07:30] 
[00:08:05] Tom: sample failure scenario — what happens if a GPU in dedicated pool OOMs mid-stream? do you checkpoint kv cache?
[00:08:12] Marcus: we maintain KV cache inline during generation; if a worker fails we can replay from last known prefix for short sessions and route to a warm fallback replica. there may be a token-level gap if the worker dies but we try to minimize user-perceived disruption with replay + fallback policies.
[00:08:35] 
[00:09:10] Ben: for our cost models we want an example of cost per 100k tokens for hosted vs dedicated committed 3-month and 12-month.
[00:09:18] Lina: sure, i'll include a cost calc sheet — hosted rate card, plus committed reserved pricing for dedicated with baseline + burst pricing. we'll add a worked example that matches your 300 concurrent stream scenario.
[00:09:30] 
[00:10:00] [00:10:45] Priya: we have multi-region requirements — EU data residency and NA. can redwood route by region and maintain identical perf?
[00:10:55] Marcus: yes region-aware routing available; however hardware availability may differ region to region, so p95s can vary — we publish performance profiles per-region and model. for strict SLOs we recommend dedicated pools in each region.
[00:11:15] Tom: whats the earliest we can get a profiling run with our prompts? we have a small sample dataset ready.
[00:11:22] Lina: if you share prompts and traces by 2/17 we can run initial token/sec and p95 streaming profile and share results by 2/20.
[00:11:30] Aisha: network egress — can we keep traffic inside our VPC for private?
[00:11:36] Jamal: private deployments support VPC peering and customer-controlled networking; data plane can be inside your network for air-gapped options.
[00:11:45] 
[00:12:40] Tom: any gotchas with long-running sessions (30+ seconds of streaming)? do kv cache sizes or memory fragmentation matter?
[00:12:47] Marcus: long sessions use more KV memory; we track KV cache per session and evict least-recent prefixes when necessary; fragmentation can be mitigated via periodic compaction in the runtime but it's uncommon. we'll surface memory profiles in the benchmark report.
[00:13:10] 
[00:13:50] Priya: ok, competitive question — why pick redwood over inferflow which is cheaper per token?
[00:13:58] Lina: good question — Redwood focuses on predictable production SLOs, observability, and rollout tools. cheaper per-token sometimes hides extra engineering cost to reach p95 targets at scale. we also offer unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private which reduces ops complexity.
[00:14:20] Ben: show us a breakdown of cost vs latency tradeoffs per model variant.
[00:14:25] Marcus: will do — the benchmarking will include cost per token at different batch sizes and the p95 impact.
[00:14:40] 
[00:15:30] [00:15:45] Tom: we may want to do a short POC: 2-week dedicated pilot with reserved capacity in NA-east to validate p95 under our 300 concurrent streams. what's the engagement look like?
[00:15:55] Lina: we can do a paid pilot — usually 2-4 weeks — we provision a dedicated pool sized for your traffic, run baseline benchmarks, and tweak batching/kv/quantization. if you want private networking we add that to scope.
[00:16:12] Aisha: pilots — are there minimum commitments?
[00:16:15] Lina: pilots are billed as short-term reserved capacity; we'll provide an estimate in the pricing doc.
[00:16:22] 
[00:16:40] Jamal: practical note, for streaming we instrument at token-level so you can see token emission distribution, first-byte timings, and per-route p95. we'll give you dashboards.
[00:16:55] Tom: that's helpful, we need per-route tracing to debug spikes.
[00:16:58] Marcus: we also provide flamegraphs for kernel hot spots if perf dives deep.
[00:17:20] 
[00:18:00] Priya: ok slightly micro question — how do you measure p95 for streaming? is it time-to-first-token or time-to-last-token?
[00:18:05] Marcus: we track both. typically SLOs are first-byte p95 for responsiveness and end-of-stream p95 for completion SLAs. you can pick both as formal SLOs.
[00:18:18] 
[00:18:50] Ben: we also have legal questions around data retention — can logs be auto-purged?
[00:18:55] Rina: yes retention policies configurable per-account; for private you can push logs to your SIEM and purge on your schedule.
[00:19:10] 
[00:19:40] [00:20:05] Tom: so next steps — benchmark with our prompt set, cost sheet, security pack, and schedule workshop.
[00:20:12] Lina: yes i'll own pricing and the security docs. Marcus you're on benchmarking and test harness.
[00:20:20] Marcus: correct, i'll prep an instrumented harness and a runbook.
[00:20:28] Priya: timeline: we want results before our internal budget meeting 3/1. is that doable?
[00:20:34] Lina: yes, if you send artifacts by 2/17, we can deliver profiling by 2/20 and a follow-up workshop the week after.
[00:20:45] Aisha: last piece — how are quotas and throttles enforced under burst?
[00:20:50] Jamal: token quotas are enforced at token-usage level with soft-throttles and hard limits. for dedicated you can set higher quotas and we have graceful backpressure with queue depth controls.
[00:21:10] 
[00:21:50] [00:22:05] Tom: one more — do you support model pinning per-route? we need deterministic outputs for some customers for audits.
[00:22:12] Marcus: yes model pinning and immutable model versions for routes are supported, plus rollout controls.
[00:22:20] 
[00:22:55] Ben: are there any performance implications for pinning older model versions?
[00:23:00] Marcus: older models might not have optimized kernels or quantization profiles, so perf may vary. we can recompile kernels for older weights in many cases but recommend pinning to vetted variants.
[00:23:18] 
[00:24:00] [00:24:15] Priya: ok, can you send a short one-pager with recommended configuration for: streaming short summaries (80-150 tokens) at 300 concurrent; and longer summaries (up to 512 tokens) at 80 concurrent?
[00:24:25] Lina: yes will do — that'll include baseline dedicated sizing, expected p95 numbers, and cost per 100k tokens.
[00:24:35] 
[00:25:10] Tom: are there any known issues with repeated prefix templates causing cache blowup?
[00:25:18] Jamal: uncommon but if you have many unique prefixes caching less effective; we recommend sharding requests by template and using shared prefix IDs when possible.
[00:25:30] 
[00:26:00] Priya: ok vendor question — do you provide per-token cost breakdown on console?
[00:26:05] Rina: yes cost and latency breakdowns per token, per-route in console, and we can give token-level traces for the pilot.
[00:26:20] 
[00:27:00] Ben: about the profiling harness — will it run in our account or yours?
[00:27:05] Marcus: for hosted we run tests in our environment with your prompt set; for private/dedicated we can run in your VPC for more realistic numbers. we'll propose both.
[00:27:20] 
[00:28:15] [00:28:30] Tom: slight tangent: does Redwood do automatic quantization suggestions?
[00:28:35] Marcus: yes Redwood Optimize suggests quantization and batching profiles by workload; it gives tradeoffs and expected regression on quality.
[00:28:48] 
[00:29:40] Priya: ok any blockers we foresee?
[00:29:44] Lina: only needing your prompt artifacts and traffic traces. also if you require HSM integration that might add procurement time.
[00:29:55] Aisha: procurement is already aware; we'll share the security questionnaire.
[00:30:05] 
[00:30:50] [00:31:10] Ben: question — what observability for kernel-level perf? we might need to correlate slowdowns to GPU util.
[00:31:18] Jamal: we expose GPU telemetry, kernel latencies, and memory stats in the trace—can correlate to tokens/sec.
[00:31:30] 
[00:32:00] Tom: can you run a stress test for 12 hours to show stability under sustained bursts?
[00:32:05] Marcus: yes we can schedule a soak test as part of the pilot, usually 6-24 hours to catch memory leaks or fragmentation.
[00:32:18] 
[00:33:00] Priya: great. time for a quick recap and commitments?
[00:33:06] Lina: recap: we will run streaming + token/sec profiling using your prompt set (deliverables by 2/20), send security pack and SOC2 docs (Lina), pricing matrix + pilot estimate (Lina), benchmarking harness and runbook (Marcus).
[00:33:25] Priya: correct, deliverables and timeline approved.
[00:33:30] Tom: thanks, we'll send the prompt set and traces by 2/17.
[00:33:36] 
[00:34:10] [00:34:30] Aisha: one last ops note — can you share the list of required IAM roles & network ports for private deployment?
[00:34:36] Lina: yes, i'll include a minimal network and IAM checklist in the security pack.
[00:34:45] 
[00:35:20] Ben: anything else?
[00:35:22] Rina: i'll follow up to schedule the profiling workshop week of 2/22.
[00:35:30] 
[00:36:05] [00:36:20] Tom: ok thanks everyone, this was useful.
[00:36:24] Priya: thanks, bye.
[00:36:27] Lina: thanks all.
